column3: “especially Jericho” renders “and Jericho”; “harlot” renders “prostitute,” and “lodged” renders “lay down.”
“had taken … hidden” uses the pluperfect; the Hebrew “hid him” is singular.
“when it was time to shut the gate” renders “the gate was about to shut.”
“stalks of flax” renders “flax of the tree.”
NASB moves “they shut the gate” to the end.
“the Red Sea” renders “the Sea of Reeds”; “utterly destroyed” renders the verb for devoting to destruction.
“dealt kindly” renders “done loyalty (hesed)”; “a pledge of truth” renders “a sign of faithfulness.”
“Our life for yours” renders “Our life in place of you to die”; “deal kindly and faithfully” renders “do loyalty and faithfulness.”
“on the city wall” renders “in the wall of the city wall.”
“Surely” renders “for”; “hands” is plural for the Hebrew singular “hand.”
